author: Linnaeus, 1766
status: 겨울철새 수백 마리 · 나그네새 수십 마리
summary: 전국에서 관찰되지만 찾아오는 수는 적은 겨울철새다. 습지와 농경지에서 홀로 지내며 주로 설치류와 새를 잡아먹는다. 세계적으로 펼쳐지는 조류 보호 운동에 힘입어 수가 차츰 늘고 있다.
young: 어린새는 암컷과 비슷하나 윗면이 더 짙고 고른 갈색이며, 아랫면과 날개 아랫면 덮깃이 붉은빛이 도는 황갈색이고 무늬가 적다.

art.subject: Hen Harrier (Circus cyaneus), adult male, as seen over Korean farmland and marshes from November to March: head, upperparts and breast pale blue-grey; a small, flat-crowned hawk's head with only a faint paler rim around the cheeks; belly, flanks and undertail coverts white; outer five primaries black, forming a broad black wingtip; a dark grey trailing edge to the secondaries; uppertail coverts white, forming a white rump patch; tail pale grey with faint bars. Bill small, black and hooked, with a yellow cere; iris yellow; legs long, thin and yellow.
art.pose: flying low over a field in side view, head in profile looking down at the ground ahead, searching for prey
art.scene: Korean winter farmland: harvested rice fields beside a marsh; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched: pale blue-grey head, upperparts and breast, white belly, black wingtips, yellow eye and long yellow legs
adult male, flight from below: white underwing and belly, black outer five primaries, dark trailing edge to the secondaries, white rump, pale grey tail
adult female, side view perched: brown upperparts, brown cheeks framed by a faint pale rim, buff underparts heavily streaked brown, white rump, long tail barred dark brown and buff, yellow eye
art.build: Slim, medium-sized raptor, about the length of a crow but much lighter, with long wings and a long tail. Small, flat-crowned hawk's head with only a slight facial ruff; in profile it looks like any hawk's head. Bill small and hooked. Legs long and slender, yellow. At rest the wingtips fall short of the tail tip. Tail long and narrow, rounded at the tip. Quarters low and slowly over fields and reeds, a few wingbeats then a glide on wings raised in a shallow V; the wings are broad-based with a blunt, five-fingered tip.
avoid: Do not paint a black head, black back or black wing bands on the male; those are Pied Harrier features.
Do not paint only a narrow black wedge of three or four primaries (Pallid Harrier); the male's black tip spans five primaries.
Do not draw a heavy, short-tailed buzzard shape; harriers are slim and long-tailed.
Do not omit the white rump on either sex.
Do not paint a round, flat, owl-like face turned towards the viewer; the facial ruff is only a faint rim, and the head is a small hawk's head with a hooked bill.
